For weeks, as Israel's election campaign has intensified, the discussion among
many has been about the "blocs" that are being formed among political parties:
specifically the Netanyahu and the anti-Netanyahu blocs. In examining the
"blocs," the focus is on numbers, on the conscription of the ultra-Orthodox
Jews, and ultimately whether this is a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu
himself. And while there's much genocidal talk, ignored is what this election
means for 50% of the population that lives from the River to the Sea:
Palestinians.

As a Palestinian citizen of Israel (who make up 16% of the eligible voters),
the election takes on a different meaning. For us, it is almost existential.
